dedupe_keys.name: tom d taking advantage of microclimate data for urban building energy modeling

description: Thomas Dougherty at Stanford University publishes the New York City inputs for the TOM.D urban building-energy study. The May 2023 ZIP archive contains building footprints, monthly building energy consumption and matched, cleaned microclimate information. The deposited description names thermal-infrared measurements, NOAA and ERA5 climate products, and preprocessed Google vision information among the sources. Download is free under CC BY 4.0. These linked observations can help calibrate building-energy simulations or compare the contribution of local microclimate variables. Exact years, building counts, units, joining keys and internal formats remain unknown from the public summary. Provenance and upstream reuse conditions need checking before redistribution of derived products. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this assembled study dataset. The archive was not downloaded, so matching quality and model results remain untested.
